title: What If Mount Everest Fell Into the Mariana Trench?

scenes.text: What if Mount Everest sank into the deepest ocean trench? It wouldn't even break the surface.
Everest stands about 8,849 meters tall. The Challenger Deep, at the bottom of the Pacific, is about 10,935 meters deep.
Set Everest on the bottom, and its peak would still sit more than a mile under the surface.
The water pressure down there is more than a thousand times what we feel at sea level.
Only twenty-seven people had reached the bottom by 2022, and the deepest dive logged was 10,927 meters.
So the tallest mountain on Earth would vanish, with a mile of ocean to spare.
